title: Manuscript Leaf from a Book of Hours
medium: Tempera, ink, and shell gold on parchment

altText: A small parchment page from a prayer book, with a painted picture of the Virgin Mary holding the Christ Child, with angels, set within a decorated frame and a block of handwritten text.

context: A single page from a Book of Hours, a prayer book for lay people, made in the Netherlands around 1500. It is painted on parchment with tempera, ink, and shell gold, and it is about 14.6 by 11.3 centimeters. The museum's tags note angels and Madonna and Child.

descriptions.k: This is one small page from a very old prayer book. A woman holds her baby. Angels are near. The page has gold paint, colorful pictures, and handwriting. Where do you see shiny gold?
descriptions.g12: This small page comes from a prayer book made in the Netherlands about 500 years ago. It was painted by hand on parchment, which is made from animal skin. A mother holds her baby, and angels are nearby. Some paint is real gold. Where do you see the pictures, and where do you see the writing?
descriptions.g35: This is one page, called a leaf, from a Book of Hours, a prayer book that ordinary families could own in the late Middle Ages. It was made in the Netherlands around 1500 and is about the size of a postcard. The artist painted on parchment with tempera, added ink for writing, and used shell gold, which is gold ground into paint. The museum notes angels and the Madonna and Child. How does the page combine picture, writing, and decoration?
descriptions.g68: Books of Hours were prayer books for lay people, and this leaf from the Netherlands, around 1500, shows why they were treasured. The artist used tempera for color, ink for the text, and shell gold, a paint made from ground gold, on parchment. The page pairs a framed picture of the Madonna and Child with angels with a block of text, so image and prayer work together. The leaf has been separated from its book. How do the picture, the border, and the text share the space, and what do we lose when a page is taken from its book?
descriptions.g910: This leaf from a Book of Hours, made in the Netherlands around 1500, shows how illuminators combined image, ornament, and text on a very small scale. The tags note angels and the Madonna and Child, a devotional subject suited to private prayer. Tempera and shell gold were applied to parchment, with gold giving the page a glowing surface that changes as light moves. Because it is a single leaf from a larger book, its original order and owner are unknown. How does the page's design guide private, close-up looking?
descriptions.g1112: A leaf from a Book of Hours made in the Netherlands around 1500, this page belongs to one of the most widely produced types of late medieval manuscript. The Madonna and Child with angels is a devotional image designed for close viewing, framed by a text block that makes it part of a prayer sequence. Shell gold and tempera on parchment create a luminous surface that depends on handling and light. Because the page has been separated from its volume, its original context and patron are lost. How should we interpret an object that was made as part of a whole but survives as a fragment?

teacherNote.context: A single leaf from a Netherlandish Book of Hours, about 1500, painted on parchment with tempera and shell gold. The record lists angels and the Madonna and Child; the original book and owner are unknown.
directions: Have students design a small page with a framed picture and a block of text, then add a border.
Use a flashlight and a piece of gold paper to show how a gold surface changes as light moves.
Discuss why people kept small books for private use and what students keep for the same reason.
